correctness.rationale: The irredundant facets after diagonal coordinate change y_i=x_i/s_i are x_i≥0 for minimal elements, x_i≤s_i for maximal elements, and x_i/s_i≤x_j/s_j for covers. The cover unnormalized normal is s_j e_i−s_i e_j, whose normalized slack exactly equals (y_j−y_i)/sqrt(1/s_i²+1/s_j²); source and sink slacks are y_i/(1/s_i) and (1−y_i)/(1/s_i). A radius-r ball satisfies precisely the augmented-DAG difference inequalities. Summing any bottom-to-top path gives 1≥r∑w, so r≤1/L. Defining longest prefixes d_− and y_i=r*d_−(i) at r=1/L satisfies all lower boundary/cover inequalities, and maximal-element upper slacks follow from d_−(i)+w(i,top)≤L; reverse suffixes produce a second center. Every center is sandwiched between r*d_−(i) and 1−r*d_+(i). Equality of both bounds for every vertex exactly characterizes uniqueness; if one strict, two constructed centers differ. n=1, antichains, unequal weights and chains all conform to proof; s=1 yields 1/[2+(h−1)sqrt2], chain yields stated reciprocal sum. Bundled five small DAG examples check DP but arbitrary-poset proof is symbolic.

value.rationale: Determines the natural standard-Euclidean inradius for every s-lecture-hall order polytope, a widely studied generalization, by an explicit O(n+|covers|) weighted longest-path computation. It additionally gives all centers, explicit lower and upper extremal centers, and a sharp graph-theoretic uniqueness criterion. The exact weight coupling s_i,s_j is metric information not inherited from ordinary order-polytope Ehrhart/IDP results, giving a practically reusable natural structural theorem.
residual_risks: Optimization proof is elementary once exact facet normals are known; scientific interest rests on application to this family and full center structure, not a new algorithmic paradigm.

final_claim: For every nonempty naturally labeled poset P and positive lecture-hall weights s, the standard Euclidean inradius of O(P,s) equals the reciprocal of the maximum augmented-Hasse path weight with source/sink weights 1/s_i and cover weights sqrt(s_i^-2+s_j^-2); prefix/suffix longest paths give explicit incenters and uniqueness iff every element lies on a maximum-weight path.
limitations: Naturally labeled, s_i>0, canonical Euclidean coordinates only.
